page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on external storage options, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.c6.xlarge in the lower tiers of tested hardware. The instance scored 1310.68 on stress-ng single-core CPU performance and 3484.23 on multi-core performance, both falling into the bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests show 194.66 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 26.23 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registered at 17.55 GB/sec, which is categorized in the bottom 10% of performance. Redis SET operations achieved 3.38 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reached 3.84 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6.xlarge offers a dedicated CPU allocation on an Intel Xeon platform, making it a predictable entry-level option for compute-bound tasks that do not require high memory-to-CPU ratios. However, the trade-off is its relatively low benchmark performance across CPU, memory, and database operations. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic batch processing, and moderate computational workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores but do not demand high-performance memory throughput or local storage.
